name: clean
why: a detector that fires on every file is not a detector
note: must produce NO findings at all

name: ascii-separate-sign
why: not every fixed-width extract is EBCDIC; some carry a real +/- character

name: packed-heavy
why: COMP-3 is two digits a byte with the sign in the final nibble; read as text it is unprintable and as a string it is truncated
note: scaled money in COMP-3 carries the same 100x trap as DISPLAY

name: corrupt-packed
why: a COMP-3 field that is not actually packed - wrong usage, or wrong offset

name: wrong-copybook
why: the copybook does not describe this file, and nothing downstream would be trustworthy if it carried on
note: scan must refuse rather than report findings

name: variable-blocked
why: RECFM=VB: every record carries a 4-byte record descriptor word
note: the 4-byte descriptor word is detected and stripped

name: never-populated
why: a reserved field carried through every migration and never used, and a code no 88-level accounts for

name: unset-numeric
why: low-values in a numeric field are 'not set', not a sign - the check that gets this wrong reports every empty indicator as a defect

name: range-condition
why: VALUE 1 THRU 5 is a range, not two values; only 7 is genuinely uncovered, and the range must not collide with VALUE 1

name: ascii-native-zoned
why: the ASCII-native sign convention: 0x70-0x79 is a negative digit, and it is not the EBCDIC overpunch nor a translation of it
note: read as EBCDIC-or-nothing this column loses every sign AND its last digit; read as cp037 it must raise UNKNOWN_SIGN_BYTE

name: float-hex
why: IBM hexadecimal float - not IEEE 754, and the difference is invisible in any single value
note: measured, not assumed: 0 of 120 values are unnormalisable

name: float-ieee
why: IEEE 754 in a COMP-1/COMP-2 field, which the default reading turns into confident numbers off by orders of magnitude
note: the discrimination pair for float-hex: same values, same copybook, one byte-level difference

name: float-ieee-le
why: little-endian IEEE 754, which is what a PC COBOL compiler writes; the format and the byte order are two separate unknowns
note: read as big-endian IEEE this still returns finite numbers
